A splenectomized patient develops fever and hemolytic anemia after a tick bite. Peripheral

(a) Malaria
(b) Babesiosis

PART-B
Q.5 A 42-year-old man with a previous history of rheumatic heart disease presents with prolonged 2+2+4+2=10
fever, fatigue and weight loss. Examination reveals a new cardiac murmur and splinter
hemorrhages:
(a) What is the most likely diagnosis and causative organism?
(b) Describe the pathogenesis of the disease.
(c) Discuss the laboratory diagnosis.
(d) Write about the treatment and preventive measures of the disease.
Q.6 Write short note on the following: 7×5=35
(a) Protective functions and clinical significance of normal microbiota
(b) Clinical manifestations and lab diagnosis of Leishmaniasis
(c) Morphological characteristics and lab diagnosis of Candidiasis
(d) Lab diagnosis and infection-control measures for Ebola virus disease
(e) ELISA - Principal and its types
(f Clinical manifestations, life cycle, and laboratory diagnosis of Trypanosoma cruzi
(g) Clinical features, pathogenesis of severe malaria, and laboratory diagnosis of Plasmodium
falciparum infection
Q.7 Multiple choice questions. 1x5=5
1. A patient develops fever, abdominal cramps and bloody diarrhoea. Stool culture shows a non-
lactose-fermenting, non-motile Gram-negative bacillus. The most likely organism is:
(a) Shigella
(b) Campylobacter
(c) Vibrio parahaemolyticus
(d) Salmonella Typhi
2. A patient from an endemic region has chronic lower-limb lymphedema. Night blood
examination demonstrates sheathed microfilariae. The likely parasite is:
(a) Dracunculus medinensis
(b) Loa loa
(c) Onchocerca volvulus
(d) Wuchereria bancrofti
3. A patient develops chronic pulmonary symptoms after inhaling fungal spores from soil
contaminated with bird or bat droppings. Which fungal infection is suggested?
(a) Histoplasmosis
(b) Candidiasis
(c) Dermatophytosis
(d) Aspergillosis
4. A family develops diplopia, dysphagia and descending flaccid paralysis after eating
improperly preserved food. The causative toxin is:
(a) Tetanospasmin
(b) Botulinum neurotoxin
(c) Shiga toxin
(d) Cholera toxin
5. A 2-year-old child develops acute watery diarrhea and vomiting with dehydration. Which virus
is the most likely cause?
(a) Norovirus
(b) Adenovirus
(c) Rotavirus
(d) Astrovirus
